observations: Only a data connection resuming the authenticated control session's TLS1.3 ticket succeeds.
A same-IP client with no ticket and a ticket from another control binding are rejected, despite the shared certificate and hostname.
A ticket before application authentication is rejected. AllowData is one-time; a closed binding cannot reopen and refuses new handshakes.
A resumed data-session ticket cannot become a fresh control connection.
Untrusted certificates, wrong hostnames, TLS1.2, unsafe/symlinked/oversized certificate or key references and mismatched keys are rejected.
Cryptographic policy and key parsing stay inside internal/crypto. PEM and temporary ticket buffers are cleared; Go-owned parsed key/ticket copies remain an explicit library boundary.

engine_review.finding: Passive sockets bind wildcard addresses before the wrapper hook; the transfer also retains the original deadline setter. This does not meet the required loopback socket lifecycle.
engine_review.next_action: Select a compatible engine or auditable licensed pinned patch with passive-address and cancellation controls; do not patch module cache. Then integrate shared custody and qualify stock explicit/implicit receiving and independent sending on GitHub.

limits: No FTP listener or client exists yet. All four FTPS parity rows remain planned; this component proves neither wire interoperability nor durable file acceptance.

The future adapter must create exactly one binding per control connection, authenticate and audit before AllowData, enforce namespace/current authority, cancel contexts and close established streams on shutdown.
Explicit/implicit sequencing, passive/active data behavior, certificate rollover, stock clients, interruption, resume, firewall/gateway operation and cross-platform execution remain unqualified.
Payload/key/clean-host recovery, active/queued upgrades, WindowsD103, all83whole rows/12full journeys, independent adoption and enterprise/release gates remain open.
